title: Sony Pictures in Talks To Revive Hollywood's Iconic Cinerama Dome and ArcLight Complex
excerpt: The studio, which acquired Alamo Drafthouse Cinema in 2024, is reportedly negotiating with property owners to resuscitate the shuttered Sunset Boulevard landmark that has sat dark since the pandemic.
body:
• Sony Pictures is in talks to take over operations of the Cinerama Dome and the adjoining 14-screen ArcLight Hollywood multiplex on Sunset Boulevard, according to reports from Deadline and the Los Angeles Times published on July 21.
  • The deal would leverage Sony's 2024 acquisition of Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, which operates 35 dine-in theater locations across North America under the Sony Pictures Experiences division.
  • The complex has been shuttered since March 2020, enduring years of delayed reopening timelines despite a 30,000-signature public petition and recent conditional-use permit approvals.

A Major Studio Steps In

Sony Pictures Entertainment is in active discussions to breathe new life into Hollywood's Cinerama Dome and the adjacent ArcLight Hollywood multiplex, Deadline reported on Monday. The Los Angeles Times confirmed that Sony and its subsidiary Alamo Drafthouse Cinema are both involved in the negotiations with property owners to take over the storied complex at 6360 Sunset Boulevard.

https://x.com/Variety/status/2079698170897203293

If a deal materialises, it would mark the most significant development in the Dome's tortured post-pandemic saga — and a bold expansion of Sony's theatrical footprint. The studio became the first major Hollywood company to own a cinema chain since the repeal of the Paramount consent decrees when it acquired Alamo Drafthouse's 35 locations in June 2024.

"We believe strongly in engaging entertainment fans outside the home in fun and distinctive ways."

— Ravi Ahuja, President and COO, Sony Pictures Entertainment (on the Alamo Drafthouse acquisition)

Six Years of Limbo

The Cinerama Dome, the world's only concrete geodesic dome theater, opened on November 7, 1963, with the premiere of Stanley Kramer's It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World. Designated a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument in 1998, it became part of the ArcLight Hollywood complex in 2002 and was widely regarded as one of the finest moviegoing experiences in the country.

When the pandemic struck in March 2020, the doors closed. In April 2021, parent company Decurion Corporation announced that all ArcLight Cinemas and Pacific Theatres locations would close permanently. While other former ArcLight sites were quickly snapped up — AMC, Regal, Amazon, and Landmark each took over various locations — the flagship Hollywood complex and its iconic Dome remained dark.

Reopening timelines were announced and repeatedly pushed back: from 2022 to 2024, then to mid-2025, then indefinitely. By April 2025, Variety reported that Decurion was unwilling to either sell or reopen the property. Filmmaker Benjamin Steinberg's grassroots Save Your Cinema campaign, which gathered over 30,000 signatures and culminated in a projection protest on the Dome's exterior in April 2026, kept public pressure on the owners but yielded no firm commitments.

"By April 2025, <em>Variety</em> reported that Decurion was unwilling to either sell or reopen the property."

"By April 2025, Variety reported that Decurion was unwilling to either sell or reopen the property."

Permit Progress and the Blue Note Signal

Behind the scenes, however, the property was quietly coming back to life. A Blue Note Jazz Club opened on a corner of the complex in August 2025, representsnting the first commercial activity at the site in years. In October 2025, Dome Center LLC filed for a conditional-use permit to sell alcohol on-site — a necessary step for any modern cinema operation.

On May 12, 2026, the Los Angeles Office of Zoning Administration approved the permit, covering the Cinerama Dome, 14 adjacent auditoriums, and a planned restaurant cafe with two outdoor dining terraces. Associate zoning administrator Tim Fargo said he was "inclined to approve" the application, while property representative Elizabeth Peterson-Gower noted that ownership had taken notice of the "extreme public interest" in reopening.

"What it proves to me is that the ownership cares greatly. That's a big undertaking and a big statement in favor of the fact that ownership cares what's there."

— Elizabeth Peterson-Gower, representative for Dome Center LLC

Why Sony and Alamo Drafthouse Make Sense

Sony's involvement through Alamo Drafthouse brings a proven operational model to the table. The Austin-founded chain, now the seventh-largest in North America by box office revenue, is known for its dine-in food service, curated programming, strict no-talking policy, and devoted community of 4 million loyalty members. Under the Sony Pictures Experiences division led by Alamo CEO Michael Kustermann, the chain has continued expanding since the 2024 acquisition.

An Alamo-operated Cinerama Dome would combine one of cinema's most hallowed venues with an exhibitor that has built its brand on exactly the kind of premium, film-lover experience the Dome historically represented. The complex's 14 additional screens would also give Sony a major Hollywood exhibition footprint — significant for a studio with upcoming tentpoles including Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian American film fans in Los Angeles, the ArcLight Hollywood's revival carries particular resonance. The complex was a go-to venue for Bollywood premieres and South Asian cultural screenings, and Alamo Drafthouse locations have increasingly programmed Indian and global cinema. A reopened Cinerama Dome under Alamo's curation-focused model could expand those offerings.

What's Next

Neither Sony Pictures nor Dome Center LLC have publicly confirmed the talks. Key questions remain around the timeline and scope of renovations — industry insiders have noted that the complex will require substantial refurbishment of its auditoriums, sound systems, escalators, fire safety systems, and concession areas after more than six years of dormancy. The Dome's projection room may also need realignment to properly display films in 70mm, a format that has surged in popularity thanks to films like Oppenheimer and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.

For now, the involvement of a major studio with a proven exhibition arm represents the most concrete hope yet that one of Hollywood's most beloved landmarks will finally reopen its doors.
